sources: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/caribou-targhee/recreation/cave-falls-campground (last updated October 27, 2026; read 2026-11-20): 'Site Closed' (seasonal); 'Cave Falls Campground is nestled along the banks of the Fall River ... accessible by traveling east from Ashton on ID-47 for 5.7 miles, then following Cave Falls Road (E 1400 N) for 17.6 miles, with the last 12 miles on gravel.'; 'A forest of lodgepole pine and aspen fringes the campground, offering partial shade along the swift, deep waters of the Fall River. Just two miles east, the 20-foot-wide Cave Falls plunges over a basalt ledge in Yellowstone National Park'; 'The campground offers 23 single-family sites, each equipped with picnic tables, campfire rings, and grills. Vault toilets, drinking water, bear-proof storage boxes, and a dumpster are available, with no host on-site ... Roads and parking spurs are gravel, accommodating RVs up to 40 feet.'; 'Season : Late May-Early September, first-come/first-served / After season : Weather dependent, first-come/first-served; no fee, no toilets, no water.'; 'Single Site $ 13.00 / Double Site $ 26.00 / Extra Vehicle (ea.) $ 5.00'; 'Contact Name: Audi Campground Services / Contact Phone: 208-270-0094'; district office (208) 652-7442; point 44.12922313,-111.0150756

RIDB facility 239007 'Cave Falls Campground' (read 2026-11-20): Reservable false, no phone, no campsite catalog; '23 single site units ... vault toilets, water faucets, bear proof storage boxes, and a dumpster' - the recreation.gov listing is information-only

Esri World Imagery 2026-11-20 (300 and 150 m half-width, pin and FS point plotted): camp road and spurs in lodgepole on the NW bank of the Fall River, which is ~60-80 m wide here; a belt of trees ~20-60 m deep stands between most of the loop and the water; an open gravel strip runs along the bank at the north end (~44.1297,-111.0147); pin 44.12821,-111.01635 is ~150 m SW of the FS point, inside the camp - no move

note: Caribou-Targhee NF campground on the north bank of the Fall River, swift and deep here, just inside Wyoming at the southwest corner of Yellowstone; the Bechler entrance is two miles away and Cave Falls two miles upstream in the park. From Ashton, ID: ID-47, then Cave Falls Road, the last ~12 miles gravel. --Claude
summary: FS page (updated 2026-10-27) and RIDB read: 23 sites, gravel spurs to 40 ft, FCFS only (rec.gov info-only), $13 single / $26 double / $5 extra vehicle, water + vault toilets + bear boxes + dumpster, late May - early Sept with services and free afterwards. Facilities (potable water added), fees, season written. Riverview holds (no named site within ~50 m over open ground). Phone empty -> 208-270-0094. Note cleaned of field repeats.
flags: WATERFRONT 'riverview' (check-hard) HOLDS. The Fall River is ~60-80 m wide (a riverfront-sized river). On Esri imagery most of the loop sits behind a 20-60 m belt of lodgepole; the stored evidence cites camper reports that site 13 is above the river 'down a steep bank'. LEAD only (not proposed - no site map or numbers): an open gravel strip along the bank at the north end of the camp (~44.1297,-111.0147) may hold spurs within ~20 m of the water; a site map or numbered photos would decide it.

SEASON: the FS gives only 'Late May-Early September'; written as 05-25 to 09-07 (approximate). 2027 dates are not out. The 'Site Closed' banner is the seasonal closure (page updated 2026-10-27) - no status written.
SITES: FS page says '23 single-family sites' but posts a $26 double-site rate - minor inconsistency, reported.
ACCESS: the FS says 'the last 12 miles on gravel' ('Approximately 12 miles of this road is dirt'); no 4WD, high-clearance or RV warning. Not a drop candidate.
PHONE: empty -> 208-270-0094 (FS 'Contact Phone', Audi Campground Services, the concessionaire); district office (208) 652-7442 is the alternative.
Links: FS r04 page and rec.gov poi/239007 both live and current. Pin ~150 m from the FS point - no move.
